episode_appearances.video_title: Brand Yourself — ABC official appearance reference
episode_appearances.pitch: Online reputation management and privacy services.
episode_appearances.offer: Robert Herjavec offered $2,000,000 for 25% equity; the other Sharks did not make an offer. Patrick Ambron declined Robert Herjavec’s $2,000,000 for 25% offer and left without a deal.

timeline.event: A New York Department of State-derived corporate record reports Brandyourself.com, Inc. was formed in Delaware on this date.
Brandyourself.com, Inc. registered as a foreign corporation in New York under document 4586562, according to a New York Department of State-derived corporate record.
BrandYourself aired in Shark Tank Season 6, Episode 23; Ambron asked for $2 million for 13.5% and rejected Robert Herjavec’s $2 million for 25% offer.
A Business Wire release launched 'HelloPrivacy by Array,' demonstrating Array control/affiliation of HelloPrivacy by this date.
BrandYourself’s current site remained active with a current team and services; Array’s corporate materials describe BrandYourself as acquired by Array and HelloPrivacy LLC as an Array affiliate.

registry_records.status: Current HelloPrivacy state standing unresolved; historical NY-derived record reports Brandyourself.com, Inc. active with a past-due statement as of late 2025
registry_records.limitation: Current BrandYourself legal policies directly identify HelloPrivacy LLC d/b/a BrandYourself. The instrument transferring/merging/converting the older Brandyourself.com, Inc. business into HelloPrivacy LLC was not retrieved, so those legal entities are not treated as interchangeable without qualification.

claims.text: BrandYourself remains operating as a consumer reputation/privacy brand under HelloPrivacy LLC and is now part of Array; the exact acquisition date and legal succession from Brandyourself.com, Inc. remain unresolved.

Array’s own corporate biography material describes BrandYourself as acquired by Array, while current Array legal materials identify HelloPrivacy LLC as an affiliate. This supports acquisition/control, but the exact transaction date, consideration, and asset-versus-equity structure were not found.

BrandYourself remains a live customer-facing brand even though HelloPrivacy’s separate product name became Privacy Protect; brand operation and product naming are therefore kept separate from corporate ownership.

episode_appearances.video_title: Brass Roots — ABC official appearance reference
episode_appearances.pitch: Snack foods made from sacha inchi seeds.
episode_appearances.offer: No Shark made an offer. The Sharks raised concerns about margins, scaling, prior-investor carryover, Gailmor’s approximately one-third ownership, and the amount of consumer education required. Aaron Gailmor left without a deal after all five Sharks declined.

timeline.event: A Delaware registry-derived corporate source reports A&C Snacks LLC was formed on this date under state file number 5338888.
Greater New Orleans, Inc. reported that Brass Roots closed a $1 million investment commitment from John B. Sanfilippo & Son, Inc. to support expansion.
Brass Roots appeared in Shark Tank Season 14, Episode 12. Gailmor asked $400,000 for 7%; all Sharks declined.
The FDA list for fourth-quarter 2024 identifies A&C SNACKS LLC DBA BRASS ROOTS in Louisiana.
Brass Roots’ official site continued to sell products and maintain a store locator, supporting active commercial operation.

registry_records.entity_name: A&C Snacks LLC d/b/a Brass Roots
registry_records.entity_number: Delaware file number 5338888 reported by a registry-derived source; direct Delaware entity record not captured
registry_records.status: Current Delaware standing unresolved; federal FDA and SEC records verify A&C Snacks LLC d/b/a Brass Roots was active in regulated/financing contexts in 2024
registry_records.limitation: Direct Delaware standing output was not captured. Federal records independently identify the legal operator as A&C Snacks LLC d/b/a Brass Roots. The on-air statement that prior investors from Gailmor’s earlier business were rolled into Brass Roots does not, by itself, prove whether the same legal entity operated both ventures.

claims.text: Brass Roots is operating under A&C Snacks LLC; Aaron Gailmor received no Shark Tank offer and therefore had no Shark deal to close.

The Shark Tank transcript records that prior investors from Gailmor’s earlier business were rolled into Brass Roots and that Gailmor owned roughly one-third of the company. The exact legal mechanism—same entity, conversion, contribution or new capitalization—remains unresolved.

An SEC-filed fund schedule establishes a SAFE investment in A&C Snacks LLC d/b/a Brass Roots. The schedule’s small carrying/fair-value figure is an accounting disclosure and is not interpreted here as proof of business failure.

Current product pages emphasize the Brass Roots brand and do not reproduce the full prior-investor/equity-capitalization discussion from the broadcast. Without a same-page historical archive, this is treated as different narrative scope rather than proof of editing or sanitization.

episode_appearances.pitch: A mobile tipping and payments service.
episode_appearances.offer: Lori Greiner and Mark Cuban jointly offered $150,000 for 15%. Maria Luna countered at $150,000 for 10% plus advisory equity; the accepted structure was reported as $150,000 for 10% plus 2% advisory equity for each of Cuban and Greiner, for 14% total. Maria Luna and Dr. Hector Rodriguez accepted the joint Mark Cuban/Lori Greiner offer structure.

timeline.event: Bravo appeared in Shark Tank Season 9, Episode 9. The founders asked $150,000 for 5% and accepted a Cuban/Greiner structure reported as $150,000 for 10% plus 2% advisory equity to each Shark.
Post-show founder/company-affiliated promotional material continued to say Bravo secured/got a deal with Mark Cuban and Lori Greiner, but did not provide executed closing evidence.
Federal trademark-derived records list first use in commerce of FAMIGO on this date by BRAVO INC.
A company press release announced that BRAVO Pay had become FAMIGO, describing a new company name and brand.
BRAVO INC. filed the FAMIGO federal trademark application; the mark later registered as No. 7208629.

registry_records.status: Current Delaware standing unresolved; current FAMIGO terms identify BRAVO, Inc. as the operator and federal trademark records identify the same Delaware corporation
registry_records.limitation: No direct Delaware entity file/standing record was captured. The 2021 public rebrand changed the customer-facing name from BRAVO Pay/Bravo to FAMIGO, while current terms continue to identify BRAVO, Inc. as the legal operator; therefore the project treats this as a brand rename, not a new successor corporation.

claims.text: Bravo announced a rebrand to FAMIGO in 2021. Current service availability and the Cuban/Greiner investment closing remain unresolved; indexed legal terms alone do not establish an operating service.

The Shark deal closing is genuinely conflicted. Contemporaneous founder/company-affiliated accounts describe securing or getting the deal, while later specialist follow-up sources state the investment never materialized. Without executed documents or direct investor confirmation, the project leaves closing unresolved.
The 2021 FAMIGO rebrand did not necessarily create a new legal entity: current terms still identify BRAVO, Inc. as the operator, and the FAMIGO trademark is owned by BRAVO INC.

Some Shark Tank follow-up pages label the appearance with production-style/legacy episode numbering rather than the broadcast Season 9, Episode 9 numbering. Broadcast episode/date evidence is preserved separately to avoid converting metadata differences into a false multiple-appearance claim.

episode_appearances.video_title: Brazi Bites — ABC official appearance reference
episode_appearances.offer: Daymond John offered $200,000 for 25% and later 20%; Kevin O’Leary moved from 20% to 15% and then 12.5%; Lori Greiner offered $200,000 for 25%, and after negotiation settled at $200,000 for 16.5%. Junea Rocha and Cameron MacMullin accepted Lori Greiner’s $200,000 for 16.5% offer.

timeline.event: An Oregon Secretary of State-derived company record reports Brazi Bites, LLC was formed in Oregon on this date under registry number 69123991.
USPTO Official Gazette material identifies BRAZI BITES LLC of Portland, Oregon as the trademark applicant.
Brazi Bites aired in broadcast Season 7, Episode 9 (production code 711). The founders accepted Lori Greiner’s $200,000 for 16.5% offer.
In an Inc. founder interview, Junea Rocha said the Lori Greiner deal accepted on air fell through.
San Francisco Equity Partners acquired a majority stake in Brazi Bites; contemporaneous trade reporting said the founders and team remained involved.
Food Dive again quoted Rocha saying the Shark Tank deal fell through, independently reinforcing the post-show deal outcome.
A Canadian government importer listing identified BRAZI BITES, LLC in Portland, Oregon, supporting continuing legal/commercial activity.
Junea Rocha publicly announced that she and Cameron MacMullin were leaving their day-to-day executive roles after 14 years; Rocha said she would remain a board member.
Brazi Bites remained commercially active through its official products/store locator, and San Francisco Equity Partners still listed Brazi Bites as a current investment.

registry_records.entity_number: Oregon registry number 69123991 reported by an Oregon SOS-derived source
registry_records.status: Reported active as of 2026-07-15 by an Oregon SOS-derived registry source; current direct Oregon registry detail not captured in this environment
registry_records.limitation: Primary federal/Canadian IP and trade records repeatedly identify Brazi Bites, LLC as the legal entity. Direct Oregon entity-detail output was not captured, so the registry number/current status rely on a registry-derived source pending primary confirmation.

claims.text: Brazi Bites is operating after San Francisco Equity Partners acquired a majority stake in 2018; Lori Greiner’s on-air Shark Tank deal fell through after filming.
The Lori Greiner deal did not close; this is supported by direct founder statements in Inc. and Food Dive, not merely by later recap speculation.

San Francisco Equity Partners’ 2018 majority investment is independently supported by contemporaneous trade reporting and SFEP’s current portfolio, which still labels Brazi Bites a current investment.

Current company-story pages emphasize the founders, products and growth but do not reproduce the failed Lori closing or the complete private-equity ownership timeline. Dated interviews and SFEP records preserve those events; without same-page archives, no claim is made that current copy was edited to remove them.

The founders’ 2024 departure from daily executive roles is not treated as a business closure or ownership exit because Rocha said she remained on the board and current SFEP/company sources show continued operation.
